acceptance: Qualification: the PR states at least 20 fully observed, would-not-escalate code PRs with zero misses, independent heavy-routing reasons per PR, actual candidate skips identified, would-select rate, escalation rate and estimated runner-minutes saved. The PRs are representative of real changes, comparison evidence is complete, and unavailable reports are not counted. Zero misses in 20 is a minimum check (about 14% one-sided 95% upper bound on the miss rate), not a reliability guarantee.

Prerequisites observed before activation: the map-ID fix is merged with an observed reconciled map (same-SHA collected ids against the published map); the map-production policy is deployed and stable; qualification was restarted after the last change to map encoding, selector semantics or freshness policy.
Selection live: full fast suite plus selected medium tests runs for a covered Python-only PR, and the full medium and correctness jobs are skipped only when all heavy carve-outs are false (observed)

Recovery path demonstrated before activation: correct culprit and revert handling, with the residual already-armed and UI-bypass merge exposure recorded; unresolved defects in that path block activation unless the owner explicitly accepts them.
Owner decision recorded: whether activation requires a hosted merge stop or accepts the documented already-armed/UI bypass exposure with an explicit operator response
Owner decision recorded: acceptable miss risk, immediate rollback trigger, named responsible operator, and whether measured eligible savings justify the added selection machinery

Rollout stop and rollback written down: the named operator restores SELECTION_SHADOW=True, reruns affected heads, and requalifies after a fix. One confirmed safety miss or lost attribution pauses rollout immediately.

Every red Trunk run during rollout is reconciled to its merged PR and head, the actual tested tree, the pre-merge selection and routing, and full Trunk evidence. Confirmed omitted-medium-test misses, omitted-gate regressions, composition failures, platform differences and unknowns are classified separately. Unavailable evidence is not zero misses. A bounded operator-owned report is enough; a new workflow is not required. Evidence is preserved before the 14-day selection-artifact retention expires.

Over the 14 days after going live, against a comparable 14-day pre-live baseline that uses the final coverage schedule and selector semantics, measured with the CI usage report: report both CI-only and all-required-check PR time-to-green, job queue time (median, p90 and the tail), and PR CI runner-minutes per comparable run with sample counts and workload mix. Target hypothesis: runner-minutes per run fall at least 40%; time-to-green and queue time stay within the owner-approved non-inferiority tolerance (the median queue is already about 3 seconds, so it cannot be required to fall). Concurrent flake fixes, shard changes and oracle changes are recorded as comparison boundaries. Trunk coverage and Trunk lanes are not changed during this window.
Owner decision recorded: the non-inferiority tolerance for time-to-green and queue time

Over the same 14 days, the Trunk push first-attempt failure rate stays at or below the classified baseline, and at most one Trunk failure a week is attributed to a selection miss by the attribution report above
context:
AMENDED 2026-10-25 from an independent second review of these plans: added hard dependencies on the map-ID fix (coverage-map-missing-comment-policy-ids-20261023, implemented in PR #3391; awaiting closing), on the scheduled-coverage item (qualification must run under the final map policy) and on the recovery path (trunk-red-stops-further-merges, trunk-dist-artifact-producer-check-flake-20261022; the arm-gate culprit fix trunk-arm-gate-blames-newest-red-run-20261022 is already done); corrected qualification to 20 fully observed would-not-escalate code PRs (a code-routed PR that always escalates shows no skipping); corrected the live behaviour (full fast suite plus selected medium tests, not selected tests only); replaced the miss-attribution criterion, because the shadow-miss report compares against full PR medium results that vanish once non-heavy routing succeeds (ci.yml:1549-1588; coverage_test_selection.py:1230-1262 reports unavailable evidence as zero misses); added rollout stop, rollback and owner decisions. Zero misses in 20 observations leaves about a 14% one-sided 95% upper bound on the miss rate, so it is a minimum check, not a guarantee. Savings estimates below are labelled as estimates. Trunk keeps running per push and unchanged during the observation window.

AMENDED 2026-10-24 from an independent review of the PR-checks versus Trunk split: this is the largest CI saving available. SELECTION_SHADOW forces escalate=True (scripts/coverage_test_selection.py:814-829), so every PR runs the full medium tier and correctness gate (32 of 40 sampled CI runs; not every PR runs the full tier, because non-code routing can skip it, heavy_tier_needed.py:176-177), and the medium tier runs up to three times per merge for heavy-routed work (PR, Trunk, Trunk coverage). Estimated saving up to about 50 runner-hours a day on the PR side (an estimate with unquantified sampling and truncation bias; it would need about 80 heavy executions a day each avoiding the sampled 37.4 minutes of medium plus correctness work, out of 61.69 runner-minutes per sampled heavy run). Waits on trunk-red-run-triage-20261024 for the baseline classification (selection misses surface as Trunk failures and the 12.7% red rate would hide them), not on the later rate target, and on the CI usage report for measurement. The repository is public, so GitHub-hosted runner minutes are free; the binding limit is the concurrency cap. Queue time and PR time-to-green are the primary success metrics, runner-minutes secondary. Priority raised to high.
description: Set SELECTION_SHADOW=False in scripts/coverage_test_selection.py only when all of these hold: the heavy-tier routing fix, the inert-path manifest and map v2 are merged; the coverage-map ID fix (coverage-map-missing-comment-policy-ids-20261023) is merged and an observed map has been reconciled against its collection; the chosen map-production policy (trunk-coverage-scheduled-not-per-push-20261024) is deployed and stable; the post-merge recovery path is usable; and at least 20 fully observed, would-not-escalate code PRs show zero shadow misses, with their independent heavy-routing reasons reported and the actual candidate skips identified. Live behaviour is the full fast suite plus the selected medium tests; the full medium and correctness jobs are skipped only when every heavy carve-out is false (infrastructure, packaging and soundness carve-outs stay independent, heavy_tier_needed.py:163-200). Record the measured would-select rate, escalation rate and runner-minutes saved in the PR; if useful skipping is negligible, keep full-tier routing and decide explicitly whether to retire selection. Restart the qualification window whenever map encoding, selector semantics or freshness policy changes (for example when Trunk coverage moves to a schedule). Closing needs a 14-day observation window after going live, so this item stays open after its PR merges.
